domain: Catholic Ecclesiology / Doctrinal History / Institutional Change
topic_summary: Analysis of Vatican II (1962-1965) as either a single coherent reinterpretation of Catholic doctrine or an overdetermined composite of multiple independent doctrinal shifts that happened to coincide temporally. The kernel question: does Vatican II represent one reading of Catholic tradition or multiple simultaneous readings that produced structurally different constraints on Church practice and authority.

key_tensions: Continuity vs rupture (hermeneutic of reform vs hermeneutic of discontinuity)
Papal primacy vs episcopal collegiality (Lumen Gentium §22-23)
Extra ecclesiam nulla salus vs ecumenical openness (salvation outside visible Church)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The deposit of faith and apostolic tradition as authoritative reference for legitimate Catholic doctrine
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Magisterial teaching authority grounded in apostolic succession and conciliar consensus
commitment_system_recognition.collapse_reason: Proposed readings (single_reinterpretation vs composite_overdetermination) do not emit structurally different constraints. Both readings accept the same doctrinal outputs (liturgical reform, ecumenism, religious liberty) as legitimate. The disagreement is historiographic (how to narrate the change) rather than structural (what constraints the change produces). A genuine kernel contest would require readings that disagree on whether specific Vatican II documents bind the faithful, or which interpretation of those documents is authoritative. Instead, this is a single constraint system with contested narrative framing.

omegas.description: The proposed kernel contest (single reinterpretation vs composite) collapses because both readings accept the same doctrinal outputs as legitimate. The disagreement is historiographic (narrative framing) not structural (what constraints bind). A genuine kernel would require readings that disagree on whether specific Vatican II documents are authoritative or how to interpret them in binding ways.

Does the SSPX/sedevacantist rejection of Vatican II constitute a fourth reading of the Catholic tradition kernel, or a rejection of the kernel itself? If the former, episcopal_collegiality_tension becomes a contested kernel with three readings (conciliar, ultramontane, traditionalist).

Is episcopal collegiality a Rope (coordination) or a Snare where papal primacy systematically overrides collegial authority? Post-conciliar history (Humanae Vitae, liturgical rollbacks, synod marginalization) suggests the latter, but this requires longitudinal data beyond the model's training cutoff.

If Vatican II is a composite of independent shifts rather than a single reinterpretation, what mechanism synchronized their temporal coincidence? Was it institutional opportunity (council as forcing function), generational turnover, or external pressure (Cold War, decolonization)? The composite hypothesis requires explaining the bundling.
